newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX aims to list coal futures contract early '98. [CORRECTED 02:47 18/07]
newsitem.headline: NYMEX aims to list coal futures contract early '98. [CORRECTED 02:47 18/07]

text.p: The New York Mercantile Exchange hopes to start trading a coal futures contract tied to the eastern U.S. market in the first quarter of 1998 (corrects from 1997), NYMEX President R. Patrick Thompson said Thursday.
Thompson said the exchange planned to submit a contract proposal to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission this fall.
"We'd hope to be able to submit the contract ... to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission late this year, possibly by October or November," he told an Energy Daily conference.
"We hope we'll be able to open the contract sometime in the first quarter of next year," he said.

The contract will be for clean-burning coal, with the quality partly defined in terms of energy (BTU) content, with delivery by barge along the Ohio River in the Huntington, West Virginia area, he said.

The NYMEX committee designing the contract chose an eastern delivery point because it considered that market more competitive than the western U.S. market, with more producers and buyers and access to the export market.

Thompson said that although coal was not yet actively traded in short-term contracts, NYMEX officials hoped that by introducing a coal futures contract into the rapidly changing coal and electricity market, that coal prices would become more transparent.
"We think we see sufficient volatility in the marketplace to justify the need for an ongoing futures contract," he said.
